'''Anomids''', pale-skinned [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] native to [[Yablari/Legends|Yablari]], were among [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] wealthiest societies, thanks to their natural technical aptitude. Anomids had long been part of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], and were seen throughout the populated galaxy as technicians, explorers, or tourists.

==Biology and appearance==
Anomids were [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] ranging from 1.7 to 1.9 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall. Anomid skin was translucent with a faint [[Color/Legends|coloring]] ranging from a light violet to a pale purple and was smooth, but wrinkled with age. They had large, slender [[Limb/Legends|hands]] with six fingers on each: two end fingers, two center fingers and two thumbs, with a sharp claw on each. The fingers were paired in twos and slightly spaced apart from the others. The [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] of the Anomids were solid, with no visible irises or pupils and have been seen in varying shades of yellow or blue. The Anomids had pointed, fin-like [[Ear/Legends|ears]] that protruded from the sides of their heads. Anomid [[Hair/Legends|hair]] was often long and well kept, and was always found in shades of black, gray or white. Some Anomids had bald domes with wrinkled skin and sparse hairs, though this could have been an effect of aging as other, presumably younger, Anomids were seen with full heads of hair. The most notable thing about Anomids' appearance was the metallic, often elaborate and aesthetic masks they wore on the bottom half of their faces. These were not [[Breath mask/Legends|breath masks]], as many offworlders might have assumed, but rather [[Vocalizer mask|vocalizer units]]. The Anomids were born without vocal cords, so many decided to adorn their faces with these machines to better communicate with [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], as learning or even understanding the six-fingered [[Anomid sign language/Legends|sign language]] of the Anomids was difficult to near impossible for most humanoids or humanoid-built [[Droid/Legends|droids]].<ref name="UAA" />

==Society and culture==
Anomids almost always wore elaborate masks which covered most of their faces. These were not breath masks, but vocalizer units. Since Anomids had no vocal cords, they relied on these vocalizer masks to communicate with other species. These masks were often elaborately customized to reflect an Anomid's social status, family origin, or profession. Among themselves, Anomids communicated using an elaborate sign language. Anomid sign language required six-fingered hands, which made it difficult for [[Human/Legends|Humans]] or Human-programmed [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droids]] to use.<ref name="GG12" />

[[File:Anomidgg12.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Anomids with vocalizers.]]

Anomids were governed by a [[Central Council (Anomid)|Central Council]], whose members were appointed by regional groups of techno-nobles, scholars, and business leaders for one to seven year terms. Their legal system was cumbersome, as laws were never repealed. Instead, new laws were added to counter or modify old ones. Offworlders often studied the intricacies of the Anomid legal system, either for ideas for their own legal systems, or as examples of what not to do.<ref name="GG12" />

==History==
Anomid civilization had a long history of pacifism and technical achievement. Though they developed [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] technology first, they did not leave their home system for a century. They finally sent probes to other systems when a drought threatened food production on their home planet, by the year [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]]. After coming across a [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] colony which could bolster the [[Yablari system/Legends|Yablari system's]] food supplies, the Anomids developed a strong interest in meeting other cultures. They soon became active members of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], learning technologies and other ideas from foreign cultures in order to benefit their society. Among the first technologies they acquired were advanced [[Ithorian/Legends|Ithorian]] agricultural techniques, for which the Anomids were always grateful. Much of the technology developed or acquired by the Anomids had to do with agriculture&mdash;food was the main export and import to the Yablari system. They were also experts in the miniaturization of computer components, though they refused to work on computers with military applications.<ref name="GG12" />

During the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], Anomid [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] discovered the blueprints for an ancient [[Columi/Legends|Columi]]-machine and intended to recreate it with modern materials.<ref name="Mission">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Archaeology|Anomid Symposium}}</ref>

[[File:Anomid_RM.png|thumb|right|200px|Anomids on [[Aris/Legends|Aris]].]]

Most Anomids were pacifists&mdash;historians believed that no major wars had ever been fought in the Yablari system. However, around [[50 BBY/Legends|50 BBY]], a nonconformist subculture developed among the younger Anomids. These nonconformists wore light, sleeveless clothes rather than the oversized robes favored by most Anomids, and rejected their traditional pacifist ideals.<ref name="GG12" /> In the years preceding the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], many Anomids living on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] were afflicted with an outbreak of [[Brainworm Rot Type A]], as were [[Wol Cabasshite/Legends|Wol Cabasshites]].<ref name="Hnn-Port Crowding Increases Virus Risks">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|51|news/13411_3.html|Port Crowding Increases Virus Risks}}</ref>

During the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] era, the Central Council was internally divided, but supported the Empire for the good of the Yablari system. [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] operatives, on the other hand, liked to befriend Anomid travelers who might be persuaded to give money to the cause. Some Rebel safeworlds used Anomid food technology to stretch limited supplies.<ref name="GG12" />

==Anomid in the galaxy==
Anomids who ventured away from their homeworld typically were rogues or nonconformists whose political ideologies clashed with that of their homeworld's Central Council. During the [[Great Galactic War]] and the ensuing [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], most Anomids sided with the Republic, while those marauders found throughout the galaxy could be found with a number of allegiances, including the [[Hutt Empire]] and [[Darth Malgus]]' [[New Empire]] in an organization known as the [[Schism Collective]]. Others sought new technologies or corporate connections which could be made in other regions of the Republic. Rarely getting involved in any form of military or defense force, [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] Anomid were drawn to the ideology of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="UAA" />
